claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 typically has a relatively coarse microstructure.
Porosity in conventionally prepared ZrB2 undermines its strength and structural integrity during service.
Reactive molten-salt-assisted borothermal reduction can form dense, single-phase ZrB2 at approximately 1800 °C.
The proposed route lowers the required formation temperature relative to conventional processing above 2300 °C.
The transient liquid phase enhances mass transport and densification during synthesis.
Molten-salt assistance increases atomic mobility and lowers reaction barriers during borothermal reduction.
Enhanced atomic mobility and lower reaction barriers promote fuller densification at lower temperature.
The proposed route produces a finer and more uniform grain structure.
Lower-temperature liquid-phase processing minimizes pore coalescence and residual defects.
Reduced porosity and refined grains increase the structural integrity of ZrB2.
Reduced porosity and refined grains improve resistance to the corrosive and mechanical effects of a liquid plating bath.
Liquid-phase-derived ZrB2 will have fewer pores than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
Liquid-phase-derived ZrB2 will have greater mechanical strength than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
Liquid-phase-derived ZrB2 will resist component failure better during prolonged liquid plating exposure.
